transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. How can I help you today?

I came in because I’ve started doing things that honestly scare me a little. Or… more than a little, I guess. I’m normally a very controlled person — I work as a systems analyst, so my whole job is planning, checking, not just reacting — but lately I’ve been doing things that feel completely unlike me.

Like, I’ll be in the middle of a deployment at work, something important where I know people are counting on me, and I just… walk out. Not because it’s finished, not because it’s fine, just because I suddenly can’t stand being there and I leave. And then afterward I think, what was I doing? That could have really messed things up.

And I’ve also been driving around late at night with no real plan. I’ll just get in the car and go, not really thinking through where I’m headed or whether it’s safe or what I’m trying to accomplish. I’m 47, I’m not someone who usually acts impulsively like that. This is not how I’ve ever handled stress before, and it’s starting to make me feel like I can’t quite trust myself.
Have you had any periods recently where you felt unusually upbeat, energized, or irritable — maybe even to the point where others noticed you were acting out of character?

I don’t think so… at least not in the way you’re describing. I haven’t had a stretch where I felt, like, unusually happy or on top of the world or full of energy in a good way.

I mean, I’ve been keyed up sometimes, and I know I’ve probably seemed tense or sharper than usual, but not upbeat exactly. And if people have noticed I’m acting out of character, I think it’s more because I seem unsettled or I’m doing things that don’t make sense for me, not because I’m suddenly energized or confident or anything like that.

I guess I’m not totally sure where the line is between irritability and just being overwhelmed, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had a period where I felt unusually energized or like I needed less sleep or was unusually cheerful. It doesn’t feel like that.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the time lately?

Yeah… I think so. I’m not sure I’d call it “depressed” in the way I used to think of that word, like crying all day or not caring about anything, but there’s been this heavy feeling most of the time.

Even on quiet days, when nothing is actually happening, I’ll have this mix of fear and shame sitting right in my chest. Like I should have handled everything better, like I somehow failed at something, and at the same time like something could still happen if I relax even a little. It’s hard to explain because it’s not always a clear thought — it’s more like my body is already convinced I’m in trouble.

So yes, hopeless maybe isn’t the exact word every minute, but I do feel worn down by it. It’s like I can’t just have a normal calm day without that background feeling being there.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies, work tasks, or spending time with people?

Yes. That’s actually been one of the more noticeable things, because I used to be… I don’t know, not wildly social every minute, but I had a life. I used to plan my week around things I genuinely liked — salsa class, book club, yoga, having people over and cooking Guatemalan food. Those were the things that made the week feel like it had shape to it.

Now I’ll agree to go, or I’ll tell myself I’m going to go, and then when it gets close I just cancel. Or I don’t answer messages right away because I know someone is going to ask if I’m still coming. And then I feel bad, because these are people I like, and these are things I used to look forward to. It’s not that I suddenly hate them. It’s more like I can’t make myself care enough in the moment to get dressed, drive there, be around people, act normal.

So I end up sitting at home, usually on the couch, scrolling on my phone or putting on a show and not really watching it. Just kind of pretending I’m doing something relaxing, but it doesn’t actually feel relaxing. It feels like I’m hiding from my own life, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed a decrease in your energy level or felt unusually fatigued lately, even when you’re not doing much physically or mentally?

Yes… definitely. I feel tired almost all the time lately, even when I haven’t really done anything to explain it.

A lot of it is the sleep, I think. Most nights I’m lying there for what feels like forever, and my mind keeps going back to pieces of what happened at the office. Not even always in a full, organized way — it’s more like little fragments, moments, sounds, things I wish I’d done differently, and then I’m awake again even though I’m exhausted.

And then when I finally do fall asleep, it doesn’t feel restful. I’ll wake up tense, either from some dream or because I heard some tiny noise in the apartment, something that probably wouldn’t have bothered me before. But my body reacts like I need to be alert right away. So by the time the alarm goes off, I already feel drained, like I’m starting the workday from below zero instead of from a normal place.

It’s frustrating because I’m not out running marathons or doing anything physically demanding. I can just be getting ready for work or sitting at my computer and already feel worn out.
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms? Have they been present most days for at least two weeks, or have they come and gone over a longer period of time?

It’s been… a lot longer than two weeks. I mean, if I’m really counting from when I started noticing I wasn’t myself, it goes back to that late-night cutover incident at work. That was a little over a year ago now — about thirteen months, I think.

At first I kept telling myself it was just a rough week, then a rough month, like once things settled down I would settle down too. But it didn’t really go away. It’s been there most days since then, in some form. Some days are less intense than others, so it’s not like every single day is exactly the same, but it hasn’t been something that just came and went for a couple weeks and then cleared up. It’s been kind of woven into everything since then.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently — like eating significantly less or losing weight without trying?

I don’t think so… not in any clear way that I’ve noticed. My appetite is maybe a little inconsistent, but I can’t honestly say I’ve been eating significantly less or that I’ve lost weight without trying.

I mean, some days I’m not that interested in food and I’ll just make something easy or snack instead of cooking a real meal, but other days I eat normally. My clothes don’t feel dramatically different or anything like that. I haven’t been tracking my weight closely, so I don’t want to say there’s been no change at all, but nothing has stood out to me as a major appetite or weight change.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, been so restless that you can’t sit still for very long?

I’m not really sure that I’ve noticed either one in a clear way.

I mean, I do feel slowed down sometimes in the sense that I’m tired and it takes me longer to get started on things, but I don’t know if I’m actually moving slowly, like if someone watching me would notice it. Nobody’s said anything like that to me.

And restless… I don’t think I’m pacing around constantly or unable to sit still for long periods. I can sit at my desk or on the couch. Sometimes I shift around or feel like I can’t get comfortable, but I wouldn’t describe it as being physically agitated all the time.

So… I guess my answer is no, not in a major or obvious way. At least not that I’ve noticed.
Have you had any thoughts about not wanting to live, or about harming yourself in any way?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had moments where I feel really overwhelmed and exhausted, like I just want everything to stop for a while, but that’s different from wanting to die or thinking about hurting myself.

I haven’t made any plans or done anything to harm myself. It’s more like… I get worn down, mentally, and I wish I could shut my brain off or not have to deal with everything for a bit. But I don’t sit there thinking, “I don’t want to be alive,” if that makes sense.

I guess I’m saying no — not thoughts of killing myself or hurting myself. Just feeling very tired of feeling this way sometimes.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things for a period of at least two weeks?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, before this got to where it is now, I did have a stretch where I just kind of stopped wanting to do things I normally enjoy. It wasn’t like one bad weekend or just being busy — it went on long enough that people noticed, and I noticed too, even if I didn’t want to call it anything at the time.

I used to sort of plan my week around things. Like salsa was a big one for me — I’d look forward to going, seeing the same people, moving around, feeling like I was out of my head for a while. And I had book club, and yoga, and sometimes I’d invite people over and cook Guatemalan food, which used to make me really happy. I liked feeding people, making a whole evening out of it.

But then I started canceling. At first I’d have excuses — work, being tired, something came up — but after a while it was more like I just couldn’t make myself care enough to go. I’d stay home and scroll on my phone, or put on a show and not really watch it. Just sit there. And it felt strange because these were things I genuinely used to enjoy, not obligations.

So… yes, I guess there was a period like that. More than two weeks, definitely.
How long ago was that previous period when you lost interest in things, and did it eventually go away completely on its own?

It’s hard for me to pin down exactly how long ago it started, because it didn’t feel like one clear day where I stopped enjoying things. It was more gradual than that. I just remember that things I used to plan my week around — salsa, book club, yoga, having people over and cooking Guatemalan food — started turning into things I would cancel.

At first I told myself it was just because I was tired or busy, but then it became this pattern where I’d stay home instead and just scroll on my phone, or put on a show and sort of pretend to watch it. Like I was physically there, but not really engaged.

And no, I don’t think it went away completely on its own. There might have been days where I made myself go to something or felt a little more like myself, but that full interest didn’t really come back all the way. It’s more like it faded and then just stayed that way.

I used to sort of plan my week around things. Like salsa was a big one for me — I’d look forward to going, seeing the same people, moving around, feeling like I was out of my head for a while. And I had book club, and yoga, and sometimes I’d invite people over and cook Guatemalan food, which used to make me really happy. I liked feeding people, making a whole evening out of it.

But then I started canceling. At first I’d have excuses — work, being tired, something came up — but after a while it was more like I just couldn’t make myself care enough to go. I’d stay home and scroll on my phone, or put on a show and not really watch it. Just sit there. And it felt strange because these were things I genuinely used to enjoy, not obligations.

So… yes, I guess there was a period like that. More than two weeks, definitely.

doctor.intent: Determine the duration and persistence of the previous depressive episode to differentiate between recurrent and single-episode depression.
doctor.question: How long ago was that previous period when you lost interest in things, and did it eventually go away completely on its own?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I used to plan my week around salsa, book club, yoga, or having people over for Guatemalan food, but now I mostly cancel and sit at home scrolling or pretending to watch a show.

patient.answer:
It’s hard for me to pin down exactly how long ago it started, because it didn’t feel like one clear day where I stopped enjoying things. It was more gradual than that. I just remember that things I used to plan my week around — salsa, book club, yoga, having people over and cooking Guatemalan food — started turning into things I would cancel.

At first I told myself it was just because I was tired or busy, but then it became this pattern where I’d stay home instead and just scroll on my phone, or put on a show and sort of pretend to watch it. Like I was physically there, but not really engaged.

And no, I don’t think it went away completely on its own. There might have been days where I made myself go to something or felt a little more like myself, but that full interest didn’t really come back all the way. It’s more like it faded and then just stayed that way.
